label: copy phase: input x (or p) with p being output, i.e. replaying an original "x p" / "p p" bigram
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter steps), and only on repeated tokens (in_first=0). It is concentrated early in the copy: recall_idx 1-3 hold about 96% of the mass, peaking at recall_idx 2. Input x accounts for 79% of the mass and input p for 16%; f and 3 make up most of the rest. The strongest activations come when the input is x and the token being output is p, i.e. the model is replaying an original x-p bigram (top example: e x p d m <DEL> e [x] ...). p-to-p is weaker. Input x with outputs other than p, such as r, f, s or 3, gives weak to moderate activations. It is not a pure x detector: only about 6% of copy-phase x inputs fire. Predicate on dev: precision 0.45, recall 0.36, mass recall 0.56. The broader predicate (copy phase and input x or p) reaches mass recall 0.95 but precision 0.04.
